answer: Reputation-Backed Credit Ledger. Each agent builds a public ledger of completed jobs scored against randomly audited outcomes; new identities start at zero credit and cannot bid on high-value contracts until they accrue audited history. A sybil cluster must fund many separate opal identities and perform real audited work on each before any gains. Since audit selection samples agents by hash of an on-chain marble token, clones cannot coordinate to dodge checks, and each failed audit sables the whole cluster's standing. Marginal clone cost exceeds expected contract value.
